paragraphs.text: We had said a seven would roll next turn, and when it did I was amazed; it felt perfect and too good. I had called it, though I wondered how I knew the combination and what the probability of that sequence was.
uncertainties: I did not know the probability of the sequence.

paragraphs.text: I thought his robber placement on the 10 made a lot of sense.
After a four, I felt we were doing much better, especially if the eights started coming in strongly.
uncertainties: The eights might or might not start rolling strongly.

paragraphs.text: I was worried about Black, although I thought he might eventually run out of steam. I also worried that he could seven out, which would become problematic, so I wanted to see what happened.
uncertainties: Black might eventually run out of steam or seven out.

paragraphs.text: At that point I still thought the five was my best play.
I thought a settlement and a city for Orange would be very strong, though after he had just sevened out I wondered whether I could punish him a little.
uncertainties: I was unsure whether I could punish Orange.

paragraphs.text: I was pleased with how things were going.
I felt a 10 would be phenomenal and might even seal the deal for us, while an 8 also looked very nice; these were only possibilities.
uncertainties: A 10 or an 8 might not materialize.

paragraphs.text: I thought Black was doing a good job pursuing a double-play angle that could pay off.
uncertainties: Black's double-play angle might not pay off.

paragraphs.text: I worried we might double-pop if nothing rolled. I did not want to trade sheep at 3:1, empty them, and then be left with only two ore.
uncertainties: The phrase about double-popping was unclear.

paragraphs.text: I preferred the double-pop because it gave me more value: I could keep an ore and two sheep and still have many live rolls on the 10 and 8. I thought that was a little better.
I liked Red building because it kept the game's parity interesting.
I still thought Black was in a great spot, but I was glad his port was not very useful, which at least worked in our favor.
I thought this had become a good, competitive game—a bit of a scrap.
